newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Asian stocks seen mixed, sideways.
newsitem.headline: Asian stocks seen mixed, sideways.

text.p: Asian stocks are expected to trade in a mixed pattern through the coming week, with corporate earnings dictating direction in most markets.
Unexciting U.S. employment data overnight on Friday failed to provide much direction for Wall Street or Asian markets.

February non-farm payrolls came in much higher than expected but the alarming report was discounted by tame wage growth. U.S. blue chips rallied with relief, but worries over a possible rate hike continues to pressure shares on both sides of the Pacific.
In Asia, red-hot Taipei issues are expected to continue reaching for dizzying heights, while sagging Thai shares are expected to continue lurching lower.

Typical of most market action in Asia now, individual bourses are trading on individual factors rather than behaving as a bloc. With a lack of obvious direction from Wall Street, most markets are expected to turn to corporate earnings or economic fundamentals for guidance, dealers said.
TOKYO - The Tokyo market's benchmark is likely to continue seeking direction this week after the Nikkei average fell below the 18,000 level for the first time in nearly a month.
Brokers said that the 225-share Nikkei was likely to hover around the 18,000 level as financial institutions sell stocks ahead of the end-March corporate book closing.
"The Nikkei average is still in the 17,000 to 19,000 range it has been in for the past few months," said Tadahiro Kamogawa, Yamaichi Securities general manager.
The Nikkei ended the week 358.26 points, or 1.93 percent, higher at 18,198.74 on Friday from 18,557.00 the previous week.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks are seen advancing modestly in the week ahead, although a tightening in the U.S. labour market suggests growing inflationary pressures and higher future interest rates in both the U.S. and Hong Kong, brokers said.
"I expect to see the Hong Kong market move up...but trade in a narrow range of 13,300 to 13,600 in advance of the Swire group results," said Charles Cheung of J&A Securities.

The Hang Seng Index closed 79.01 points lower at 13,337.35 on Friday, though off a day-low of 13,304.24. During the week, the index shed 61.37 points, or 0.5 percent, on heavy average daily turnover of HK$10.81 billion.

BANGKOK - More weakness is expected in the Stock Exchange of Thailand (SET) Index on further doubts about the Thai finance sector and nervousness about a possible downgrade of Thailand's long-term sovereign debt ratings, traders said.
Despite foreign and mutual fund buying on Friday that helped lift the index more than two percent, the SET fell 36.11 points, or 4.96 percent, over the week to close at 691.45.

Thailand's largest finance group, Finance One, has announced a merger with Thai Danu Bank, a move seen as tackling Finance One's liquidity problems. On Monday, the central bank halted trading in all bank and finance stocks and slapped stringent provisioning requirements on banks and finance firms.
"I think it is going to continue going down like this until the end of the month," said a trader at Asia Credit.
BOMBAY - Indian shares are expected to consolidate gains after prices rose 16 percent following the announcement of a market-friendly 1997/98 (April-March) budget.
"The market will stop for a breather," said Govind Agarwal of at Motilal Oswal. "But the underlying sentiment is bullish."
The Bombay exchange index ended the week 18.55 points, or 0.48 percent, higher at 3,876.04.
DHAKA - Shares on the Dhaka Stock Exchange were bearish much of last week over opposition threats of political unrest, but investors were expected to return this week.

"We expect fresh (investor) commitments after panic selling set off by looming threats of political unrest. We noticed some recovery in pre-weekend sessions and the sentiment could bolster next week," one analyst said
The DSE all-share index closed at 1,541.27 on Saturday, down from the previous Saturday's 1,660.21 finish.
KUALA LUMPUR - Malaysian stocks are expected to see volatile trading in the week ahead with major players sidelined.
Ralph Dixon of TA Securities' international division said investors may sit out on Monday because of the uncertainty over how the requoted DRB-Hicom and Yahaya-related stocks perform.
The benchmark Composite Index closed the week 19.46 points higher, or 1.53 percent, at 1,251.21 on Friday, and up 1.37 points, or 0.11 percent, from Thursday.

JAKARTA - Jakarta share prices are seen mixed, although continued bargain-hunting in blue chips could push the index higher, while local investors were likely to continue buying medium and small stocks that were the subject of rumours or expected to report higher 1996 earnings.
On Friday, the Jakarta composite index closed up 0.70 points at 683.81 points. On the week it fell 21.56 points, or 3.1 percent, from the previous Friday's close of 705.37 points.
MANILA - Philippine shares are seen drifting in a narrow band during the coming week with little domestic news expected.
"But some investors on the lookout for the interest rate scenario in the United States may be kept at bay," said Sun Hung Kai Securities research head Raul Ruiz.
Traders said Equitable Bank's initial public offering will continue to sap the market's liquidity.
The main index closed at 3,286.45 on Friday, down 28.83 points, or 0.87 percent, from the week-ago 3,315.28 level.
SEOUL - Seoul stocks are expected to remain weak as sagging market fundamentals are unlikely to recover, brokers said.

"Sentiment will be weak because interest rates are rising and customer deposits with securities houses are falling. But steep falls are unlikely as investors are awaiting more concrete steps to correct the real-name financial system," said Koh Kyong-bae of Hyundai Securities.
Brokers said the composite index would move in a 650-700 range this week. The index ended at 675.07 on Saturday from 676.53 on Friday a week ago. Saturday, March 1, was a holiday.
SINGAPORE - Singapore stocks are expected to stay flat waiting for more companies to release their corporate earnings.
"The results so far are not inspiring. And there could be some more surprises on the downside especially from the Keppel group," said a broker with a local firm.

Dealers said the relisting of Malaysia's DRB/Proton group of companies, suspended last week because of the death of company chief Yahaya Ahmad, could also affect Singapore's over-the-counter market for Malaysian shares.
The benchmark Straits Times Industrial index ended at 2,178.27 on Friday, down 17.43 points over the previous week.
SYDNEY - Australian shares were seen mixed with Wall Street to set the early tone but with attention remaining on individual corporate results.
The All Ordinaries index closed at 2,438.5, down 0.4 percent from Thursday and down 0.5 percent over the week.
"Wall Street will still be the early lead but the results really do help sort the wheat from the chaff," said a broker.
TAIPEI - Taiwan share prices are seen firmer on comments by the central bank and investors' expectation for further gains.
The benchmark index rose four straight days last week on expectations of an extended economic recovery and abundant liquidity under the central bank's loose monetary policy.
Share prices on Wednesday closed at a six-year high of 8,019.46, and rose further on Thursday and Friday, when it closed at 8,162.68, its highest since 8,569.55 on May 15, 1990.
"As long as the government does not take any new actions to restrain the market despite the sharp rallies, the bullish sentiment will remain," said Oliver Fang of National Securities.
For the week, the index rose 198.73 points, or 2.49 percent, to 8,182.44 on Saturday against 7,983.71 last week.
WELLINGTON - New Zealand shares would continue to tread water with wholesale interest rates remaining high and all eyes on the Reserve Bank's six-monthly economic projections next Thursday.
"It'll be a major focus for the market, but it'll have to be something of a major statement before anything changes," said Tim Snedden at ANZ Securities.
The NZSE-40 capital index closed at 2,288.96, up 9.63 points, or 0.42 percent, from the previous Friday's 2,279.33 close.
